key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL over days to weeks (not acute or sudden). Chronic, progressive pattern. LOCATION: LOWER ABDOMEN, diffuse. Cramping throughout lower belly (not localized). DURATION: Symptoms persist for days to weeks. Cramping episodes last minutes to hours, come and go. CHARACTER: CRAMPY, ACHY abdominal discomfort. NOT sharp or stabbing. Dull, bloating sensation. AGGRAVATING: Eating may worsen bloating. Straining worsens discomfort. RELIEVING: Bowel movement or PASSING GAS provides significant relief. Fiber, hydration, laxatives help. TIMING: INTERMITTENT cramping that comes and goes. Better after defecation, worse when haven't gone for days. SEVERITY: 3-6/10, mild to moderate discomfort (not severe). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: BLOATING, sensation of incomplete evacuation, straining, HARD PELLET-LIKE STOOLS, NO bowel movement for 3-7+ days. Usually NO fever, NO vomiting. KEY POSITIVES: Gradual onset, able to pass gas (unlike obstruction), pain relief after defecation, chronic pattern, poor fiber/water intake. KEY NEGATIVES: SUDDEN onset with inability to pass gas suggests obstruction. Vomiting uncommon. SEVERE pain suggests alternative.

red_flags: Sudden onset severe constipation with vomiting - possible bowel obstruction, needs urgent imaging
Complete inability to pass gas - suggests obstruction not simple constipation
Blood in stool with weight loss - concern for colon cancer, needs colonoscopy
New onset constipation in elderly - higher risk of serious pathology
